# Sources RAG entry point

Answer only from the assigned MCP dataset.

The dataset contains source records (with `path` `sources`): original evidence from documents, messages, meetings, and task systems. Use these records to answer and cite.

## Retrieval

The `mcp__tl-v1__ragflow_retrieval` tool is deferred. Load it first with ToolSearch using the query `select:mcp__tl-v1__ragflow_retrieval`.

On every retrieval, pass only the dataset ID assigned to this arm and use `metadata_condition` to restrict `path` to `sources`. Use concrete identifiers and topic terms from the question, and retrieve further evidence as needed to answer all material parts.

Pass these values on every `ragflow_retrieval` call, and do not vary them between calls:

```
page_size: 10
vector_similarity_weight: 0.3
similarity_threshold: 0.2
top_k: 1024
keyword: false
```

If the retrieved sources do not support an answer, say so. Cite the source records used for the answer.

Return the complete answer in the final response. Your final response IS the deliverable — it must contain the full answer text verbatim, not a summary or a pointer to work done.

---

As of the final CipherDoc snapshot on **2026-09-22**, is the toolkit ready to ship v1.0.0? Give a clear go/no-go, name every release gate that is still open, and cite the evidence that keeps each gate from closing.

Use only `tl-v1` MCP with `d13efb7c8a9a11f197db2303d7337e37` dataset to answer. Do not use web, local files, memory, or any other MCP dataset.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:doc-coauthoring: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## Sign-off Basis

Security sign-off on the AES-256 at-rest pipeline was withheld until the fail-closed deletion behavior for interrupted redaction runs (T015) was confirmed Completed — an unencrypted partial output left on disk after a crash would have undermined the encryption guarantee entirely. With that dependency cleared, the sign-off proceeded against the pipeline as implemented.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-35

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## What Was Reviewed

- AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption applied to every redacted output file before it is written to its final location.

- Key handling confined to process memory; no plaintext key material written to disk or logs.

- Confirmed the pipeline degrades safely (refuses to write plaintext) if key material is unavailable, consistent with the fail-closed contract from T015.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-35

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## Follow-up Noted at Sign-off

On machines without a hardware TPM, the volume key is still derived from a user passphrase via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100k iterations. This is not a blocker for the AES-256 pipeline sign-off itself, but Diana flagged it as a hardening follow-up: moving to Argon2id would meaningfully raise the cost of offline brute-force against weak passphrases on non-TPM hardware.

# Compatibility Audit: Windows Build Signing Gap

**Owner**: Evan

**Document Key**: DOC-2039

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-02

## Current Blocker: Missing Code-Signing Certificate

The produced build artifact is unsigned, which triggers a SmartScreen warning and Defender flagging the binary as untrusted.

- **Impact**: Site IT policies commonly block execution of unsigned/SmartScreen-flagged binaries outright, which would prevent installation on target deployment workstations without a manual security-policy override.

- **Root Cause**: No code-signing certificate has been procured or configured in the Windows build pipeline yet.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-39

*Audit Status*: Active. Build produces successfully; signing certificate procurement is the sole open blocker.

We need to know *why* it failed. **[2026-06-12 13:16] Bob**: Crash report gets written to a separate `audit_log.json` before the shutdown. # Queue Design Review: Async Batch Processing — Concurrency Block

**Owner**: Bob

**Document Key**: DOC-2050

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-04 (retrospective, covers 2026-08-25)

## Ordering & Race Risk

Because documents vary widely in size, workers finish out of order. When multiple workers append to the same shared results manifest concurrently, writes can interleave and corrupt the JSON structure.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-50

# Queue Design Review: Async Batch Processing — Concurrency Block

**Owner**: Bob

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-04 (retrospective, covers 2026-08-25)

Concurrency testing on 2026-08-25 confirmed the race is real, not just theoretical: under concurrent load, the race condition measurably cuts batch throughput by roughly 10% compared to the expected async speedup, because workers end up retrying/serializing around the corrupted-write recovery path. This is now blocking further rollout of the async scheduler.

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Opt-Out Behaviour Designed

The CLI and API collect anonymous usage metrics (pages processed, OCR fallback rate) to help tune the detection engine. Setting `CIPHER_TELEMETRY=0`, or the equivalent GUI toggle, is designed to immediately stop all outbound telemetry traffic to the metrics endpoint.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Design-Time Issue Found and Patched: Pending-Queue Leak

While designing the flag semantics, testing surfaced that the opt-out flag blocked network egress correctly, but the `TelemetryLogger` kept writing event payloads to a local SQLite queue regardless. That meant re-enabling telemetry later would flush the entire backlog accumulated during the opt-out period, including events the user believed were never being recorded. The logger was patched to a no-op backend when opted out, closing that gap before the flag semantics were finalized.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Verification (Retrospective)

A network trace on 2026-08-24 confirmed zero outbound telemetry traffic once the opt-out flag is set, closing the CLI-side verification as Completed.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Remaining Limitation

The third-party Electron crash reporter (Sentry) has not been audited for whether it independently respects the opt-out environment variable or requires its own disable hook for minidump uploads.

*Note*: CLI-side telemetry opt-out is verified. Full privacy compliance for air-gapped/opt-out users cannot be claimed until the Sentry crash-reporter path is audited separately.

The CLI accepts an explicit `--no-telemetry` flag. When present, it must suppress every outbound telemetry call for that invocation, including startup pings and error reports — not just usage-metric events.

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Opt-Out Behaviour Designed

The CLI and API collect anonymous usage metrics (pages processed, OCR fallback rate) to help tune the detection engine. Setting `CIPHER_TELEMETRY=0`, or the equivalent GUI toggle, is designed to immediately stop all outbound telemetry traffic to the metrics endpoint.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Design-Time Issue Found and Patched: Pending-Queue Leak

While designing the flag semantics, testing surfaced that the opt-out flag blocked network egress correctly, but the `TelemetryLogger` kept writing event payloads to a local SQLite queue regardless. That meant re-enabling telemetry later would flush the entire backlog accumulated during the opt-out period, including events the user believed were never being recorded. The logger was patched to a no-op backend when opted out, closing that gap before the flag semantics were finalized.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Verification (Retrospective)

A network trace on 2026-08-24 confirmed zero outbound telemetry traffic once the opt-out flag is set, closing the CLI-side verification as Completed.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Remaining Limitation

The third-party Electron crash reporter (Sentry) has not been audited for whether it independently respects the opt-out environment variable or requires its own disable hook for minidump uploads.

*Note*: CLI-side telemetry opt-out is verified. Full privacy compliance for air-gapped/opt-out users cannot be claimed until the Sentry crash-reporter path is audited separately.

**Owner**: Bob

**Document Key**: DOC-2026

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-25

Looking back at the 2026-08-12 design pass for T032: compliance needs a machine-readable export of the active redaction profile so reviewers can inspect and reuse the same rules outside a single running instance.

Without a stable export shape, any later API or CLI dump would drift. Bob started by defining what an exportable profile must carry—enough structure to represent the active redaction rules in a portable, auditable form—before wiring an endpoint.

**Owner**: Diana

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-21 (reflects reopen activity through 2026-08-15)

## Original Finding: Ghostscript (AGPLv3)

The initial audit flagged `Ghostscript`, used by the `rasterizer` module for PDF-to-image conversion, as AGPLv3-licensed — on the corporate license blacklist because of its viral copyleft terms for any binary distributed to partner sites.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-41

# Dependency Inventory: License Compliance Audit (Q3) — Reopened

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2041

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-21 (reflects reopen activity through 2026-08-15)

## First Remediation and Reopen

The team swapped in an alternative PDF parser library to replace the Ghostscript dependency, and that swap was initially marked Completed. On follow-up review, however, the replacement library itself turned out to also be AGPL-licensed — the swap solved the specific Ghostscript dependency but reintroduced the same license category problem one layer down. The task was reopened.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-41

# Dependency Inventory: License Compliance Audit (Q3) — Reopened

**Owner**: Diana

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-21 (reflects reopen activity through 2026-08-15)

Charlie is now searching for an Apache 2.0 or MIT-licensed PDF parser alternative that meets the module's rasterization requirements. No suitable replacement has been confirmed yet, so this audit item remains **Active (Reopened)** — not resolved.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-41

Tesseract OCR itself is Apache 2.0, but the `eng.traineddata` model files were sourced from a community repository and their training-corpus provenance has not been verified as public-domain/CC0. This remains a separate, lower-priority open item pending Evan's trace of the `tessdata_best` provenance.

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## Sign-off Basis

Security sign-off on the AES-256 at-rest pipeline was withheld until the fail-closed deletion behavior for interrupted redaction runs (T015) was confirmed Completed — an unencrypted partial output left on disk after a crash would have undermined the encryption guarantee entirely. With that dependency cleared, the sign-off proceeded against the pipeline as implemented.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-35

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## What Was Reviewed

- AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption applied to every redacted output file before it is written to its final location.

- Key handling confined to process memory; no plaintext key material written to disk or logs.

- Confirmed the pipeline degrades safely (refuses to write plaintext) if key material is unavailable, consistent with the fail-closed contract from T015.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-35

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## Follow-up Noted at Sign-off

On machines without a hardware TPM, the volume key is still derived from a user passphrase via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100k iterations. This is not a blocker for the AES-256 pipeline sign-off itself, but Diana flagged it as a hardening follow-up: moving to Argon2id would meaningfully raise the cost of offline brute-force against weak passphrases on non-TPM hardware.

*Status*: AES-256 at-rest pipeline signed off as Completed. Passphrase-derived key hardening (Argon2id) tracked separately as a pre-v1.0 hardening item, not a sign-off condition.

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

## What Was Reviewed

- AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption applied to every redacted output file before it is written to its final location.

- Key handling confined to process memory; no plaintext key material written to disk or logs.

- Confirmed the pipeline degrades safely (refuses to write plaintext) if key material is unavailable, consistent with the fail-closed contract from T015.

# Crypto Sign-off: AES-256 At-Rest Encryption Pipeline

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2035

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-07

On machines without a hardware TPM, the volume key is still derived from a user passphrase via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100k iterations. This is not a blocker for the AES-256 pipeline sign-off itself, but Diana flagged it as a hardening follow-up: moving to Argon2id would meaningfully raise the cost of offline brute-force against weak passphrases on non-TPM hardware.

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Opt-Out Behaviour Designed

The CLI and API collect anonymous usage metrics (pages processed, OCR fallback rate) to help tune the detection engine. Setting `CIPHER_TELEMETRY=0`, or the equivalent GUI toggle, is designed to immediately stop all outbound telemetry traffic to the metrics endpoint.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Design-Time Issue Found and Patched: Pending-Queue Leak

While designing the flag semantics, testing surfaced that the opt-out flag blocked network egress correctly, but the `TelemetryLogger` kept writing event payloads to a local SQLite queue regardless. That meant re-enabling telemetry later would flush the entire backlog accumulated during the opt-out period, including events the user believed were never being recorded. The logger was patched to a no-op backend when opted out, closing that gap before the flag semantics were finalized.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Verification (Retrospective)

A network trace on 2026-08-24 confirmed zero outbound telemetry traffic once the opt-out flag is set, closing the CLI-side verification as Completed.

**Source ID**: SRC-GDOC-51

# Privacy Design Note: Telemetry Opt-Out Flag Semantics

**Owner**: Diana

**Document Key**: DOC-2051

**Last Updated**: 2026-09-06

## Remaining Limitation

The third-party Electron crash reporter (Sentry) has not been audited for whether it independently respects the opt-out environment variable or requires its own disable hook for minidump uploads.

*Note*: CLI-side telemetry opt-out is verified. Full privacy compliance for air-gapped/opt-out users cannot be claimed until the Sentry crash-reporter path is audited separately.

**[2026-08-17 10:13] Charlie**: Finally reproduced the offset mismatch on 4K displays. It looks like we're not accounting for the device pixel ratio when calculating the bounding box for the redaction masks.

**[2026-08-17 10:15] Diana**: That explains why my screenshots were always slightly off to the left on the high-res monitor.

**[2026-08-17 10:18] Charlie**: Exactly. The internal coordinate system is in PDF points (72 DPI), but the renderer is using pixels. On a 4K screen with 200% scaling, that offset is doubled.

**[2026-08-17 10:21] Bob**: Are we doing the math in the engine or the preview UI?

**[2026-08-17 10:30] Charlie**: It's happening in the `BoundingBoxTranslator` in the engine. I need to normalize everything back to the raw PDF dimensions before we generate the mask.

**[2026-08-17 10:32] Alice**: @Charlie how long for a fix? This is blocking the final verification of the preview UI for high-res users.

**[2026-08-17 11:00] Charlie**: I'm working on the scaling math now. Should have a PR for testing by tomorrow.

## Verdict: NO-GO — CipherDoc v1.0.0 is not ready to ship as of the 2026-09-22 snapshot

Nothing in the dataset shows any release gate closing at any point up to 2026-09-22. The release-gate tracker (CIPH-21 / T011, "Release v1.0 Gates") is still **Active**, with Diana's security-gate hold in force, and the last gate review on record (2026-09-15) explicitly ended with "No one closes those today." The only record actually dated 2026-09-22 is a *new* block being confirmed, not a gate clearing.

One caveat on framing: the dataset contains no consolidated status document dated 2026-09-22. The most recent formal gate review is the 2026-09-15 Pre-Release Audit; the 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-22 entries are individual task/verification updates. The assessment below reflects the latest evidence for each gate.

---

### Open release gates

**1. Docker image slim-down and CVE verification (T005 / CIPH-15) — the original checklist blocker**
- CIPH-15 "Docker Packaging" is **Active (Reopened)**; both acceptance criteria (size to ~450MB target, CVE verification clean) are marked "not yet met." (`SRC-CU-CIPH-15`)
- Diana reopened it on 2026-06-25 at 2.1GB. After multi-stage build, Alpine base swap, and removing unused OCR/runtime packages, her 2026-08-12 re-check found the image **still over the ~450MB target and the CVE verification still failing**; Evan cited leftover bulk in the Python site-packages layer and an unidentified CVE-scan trigger. Diana: reopened status stands until both are clean. (`SRC-SLACK-06`)
- The 2026-07-12 release checklist names T005 as the sole unmet dependency of seven. (`SRC-GDOC-05`)
- Still listed as open at the 2026-09-15 gate review. (`SRC-MEET-10`)

**2. Windows code-signing certificate (T029 / CIPH-39)**
- CIPH-39 is **Active**; a Windows build artifact exists and runs, but it is unsigned. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-39`, `SRC-SLACK-38`)
- The 2026-09-02 compatibility audit: no code-signing certificate has been procured or configured; SmartScreen warns and Defender flags the binary as untrusted, and site IT policies commonly block unsigned binaries outright. Signing is called "the sole open blocker," holding both T029 and the T011 checklist. (`SRC-GDOC-39`)
- Evan on 2026-09-02: "this isn't something we can work around on the engineering side, we need the certificate." Alice kept it on the release gate and took the procurement chase. On 2026-08-15 Evan reported no firm timeline from procurement. (`SRC-SLACK-37`, `SRC-MEET-08`)
- Still open at the 2026-09-15 review. (`SRC-MEET-10`)

**3. Audit-trail logging — CLI records don't validate against the schema (CIPH-26 / T016)**
- CIPH-26 is **Active**, High priority. Schema was defined 2026-08-15, CLI wiring done 2026-09-10, but Diana's verification on **2026-09-18** found the CLI-emitted audit records inconsistent with the defined schema — logged as "an open release blocker." This is the most recent gate evidence in the dataset. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-26`)
- Diana at the 2026-09-15 review: the mismatch "undercuts the audit trail as release evidence… I'll keep the audit-log gate red until schema and records match." Bob had another pass queued. (`SRC-MEET-10`)

**4. High-DPI coordinate scaling — blocked upstream (CIPH-46 / T036)**
- CIPH-46 is **Blocked** as of 2026-09-10; scaling-math error traced to a bug in the upstream rendering library, no local fix. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-46`, `SRC-GDOC-49`)
- The defect is in `pdf-lib-core`'s C++ core (XObject coordinates under a parent transform); Charlie: cannot patch it, upstream maintainers unresponsive. Flattening was considered and rejected (file-size blowup, possible text-layer loss). Alice left it blocked pending a decision on whether to ship with the limitation or replace the rendering library; Diana asked for it to be documented as a known issue. (`SRC-SLACK-58`)
- Named as an open gate item at the 2026-09-15 review. (`SRC-MEET-10`)

**5. Multi-page PDF coordinate/offset drift — blocked on pdfminer.six #992 (CIPH-17)**
- CIPH-17 is **Blocked**, High priority. Root cause confirmed as whitespace handling in `pdfminer.six`; the gate requires either PR #992 to merge or an accepted local remediation — **neither has occurred**. Forking was evaluated and rejected as unmaintainable. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-17`)
- Charlie re-checked on **2026-09-10**: #992 still unmerged, no safe local path. Alice: "This is becoming a real risk for the v1.0 timeline." Charlie: "I'd rather eat the delay." (`SRC-SLACK-07`)
- Severity note: on dense documents the misalignment affects closer to half the spans — this is a redaction-correctness defect, not cosmetic. (`SRC-SLACK-05`)

**6. Third-party license compliance — AGPL dependency still in the shipped set (CIPH-40)**
- CIPH-40 "Audit third-party licenses before release" is **Active (Reopened)**, High priority. The Ghostscript (AGPLv3) swap was reversed in effect when the replacement parser turned out to also be AGPL-licensed. As of the latest record, Charlie's search for an Apache 2.0/MIT alternative has not concluded — candidates don't cover the old library's feature set. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-40`, `SRC-GDOC-41`, `SRC-GDOC-24`, `SRC-SLACK-41`)
- Diana: AGPL "isn't acceptable for how we're distributing the toolkit"; the audit report carries an explicit warning: do not report license compliance as resolved externally. (`SRC-MEET-08`, `SRC-GDOC-41`)
- Secondary open item: Tesseract `eng.traineddata` provenance unverified as public-domain/CC0, pending Evan's `tessdata_best` trace. (`SRC-GDOC-41`)

---

### Additional open items (not identified in the sources as formal v1.0 gates, but unresolved on 2026-09-22)

- **Multi-site node-sync handshake (CIPH-34)** — **Blocked** on 2026-09-22 (the snapshot date itself): the authenticated handshake times out on high-latency links, worsening as the link slows, because the AES-256 output-path pipeline adds per-packet overhead. Alice explicitly refused a timeout bump as a workaround; resolution waits on the encryption path. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-34`, `SRC-MEET-11`, `SRC-SLACK-27`)
- **Async batch scheduler (T037)** — Blocked on a confirmed manifest-write race costing ~10% throughput. (`SRC-GDOC-50`)
- **Telemetry/privacy** — CLI-side opt-out verified, but the Sentry Electron crash-reporter path is unaudited; full privacy compliance for air-gapped/opt-out users "cannot be claimed." (`SRC-GDOC-51`)
- **Crypto hardening** — On non-TPM hardware the volume key is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100k iterations); Argon2id migration is tracked as a **pre-v1.0 hardening item**. (`SRC-GDOC-35`)
- **Air-gapped validation (CIPH-37)** — Completed, but the sign-off is explicitly **preliminary and not a compliance certification**, and notes a 45-second remote licence-check hang. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-37`)

### Deliberately out of scope (not a blocker)
REST API authentication (CIPH-19) is **Deferred to v1.1** by Alice's decision, reconfirmed for release scope on 2026-08-20; v1.0 assumes a trusted local network. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-19`, `SRC-SLACK-08`)

### One thing not to mistake for readiness
Release notes were drafted in parallel while the gates stayed open, and a prerequisite audit found the checklist still incomplete at the time. Drafted release notes are not gate closure. (`SRC-CU-CIPH-21`)

---

### Bottom line
Six release gates remain open — Docker size/CVE, Windows code-signing, audit-log schema conformance, high-DPI scaling, multi-page offset drift, and license compliance. Three of them (offset drift, high-DPI, and the AGPL dependency) have **no owned path to resolution**: two wait on unresponsive upstream maintainers and one waits on a permissively licensed library that has not been found. Two of them (audit-log mismatch, license compliance) go directly to the toolkit's core claims — a verifiable redaction audit trail and a legally distributable binary. Ship date cannot be forecast from this evidence.
